# Aligning Table Captions to the Left in LaTeX (Without `caption` Package)

Here are several methods:

## Method 1: Redefine `\@makecaption`

You can redefine the internal caption-making command in your preamble:

```latex
\makeatletter
\long\def\@makecaption#1#2{%
  \vskip\abovecaptionskip
  \sbox\@tempboxa{#1: #2}%
  \ifdim \wd\@tempboxa >\hsize
    #1: #2\par
  \else
    \global\@minipagefalse
    \hb@xt@\hsize{\box\@tempboxa\hfil}%  <-- left-aligned
  \fi
  \vskip\belowcaptionskip}
\makeatletter
```

The key change is `{\box\@tempboxa\hfil}` instead of the default `{\hfil\box\@tempboxa\hfil}`.

## Method 2: Use `\captionsetup` with `floatrow` or manual raggedright

```latex
\usepackage{floatrow}
\floatsetup[table]{capposition=top}
\floatsetup{captionpos=left}  % or use justification options
```

## Method 3: Simple Workaround with a Minipage

```latex
\begin{table}[h]
  \begin{minipage}{\linewidth}
    \raggedright
    \caption{Your caption text here}
    \label{tab:example}
    \centering
    \begin{tabular}{|c|c|c|}
      \hline
      A & B & C \\
      \hline
      1 & 2 & 3 \\
      \hline
    \end{tabular}
  \end{minipage}
\end{table}
```

## Method 4: Manual Caption (Full Control)

Skip `\caption` entirely and format it yourself:

```latex
\begin{table}[h]
  \raggedright
  \textbf{Table 1:} Your caption text here
  \par\medskip
  \centering
  \begin{tabular}{|c|c|c|}
    \hline
    A & B & C \\
    \hline
    1 & 2 & 3 \\
    \hline
  \end{tabular}
\end{table}
```

> **Note:** Method 4 won't auto-number or appear in the List of Tables.

---

**Recommendation:** Method 1 is the most robust if you truly can't use any packages — it modifies the default behavior globally. Method 3 is the quickest practical fix.
